abstract_channel_theorem.local_authority: lambda_G(c,f)=1+nu(X) for every valid exact-channel representation

reachability_normal_form.authority: Every feasible fixed triple has a distributive lattice of decompositions with canonical R_min and R_max.

definitions.representation: Any valid exact-channel decomposition of the same finite graph G with anchors c,f, possibly with different hub z, partition L/R, canonical port sets, and channel graph X.
definitions.fixed_triple_family: For fixed feasible (z,c,f), let R_lattice be the full family of feasible R-sides from the implication normal form.
definitions.anchor_pair_invariant: For an exact-channel representable ordered anchor pair (c,f), define rho_G(c,f):=lambda_G(c,f)-1.

fixed_triple_invariance.statement: For fixed feasible (z,c,f), every feasible decomposition R in the implication lattice has the same matching number nu(X_R).
proof: For every feasible R, the abstract exact-local channel theorem applies to the resulting exact-channel graph X_R.
The graph G and anchors c,f are fixed, so lambda_G(c,f) is independent of R.
Therefore nu(X_R)=lambda_G(c,f)-1 for every feasible R.
fixed_triple_invariance.formula: For all R1,R2 in R_lattice: nu(X_R1)=nu(X_R2)=rho_G(c,f).

fixed_anchor_invariance.statement: For fixed graph G and fixed exact-channel representable anchors (c,f), every valid exact-channel representation has the same channel matching number, even if the hub z and partition change.
proof: Take any two valid exact-channel representations with the same anchors c,f, possibly through distinct hubs z1,z2.
Apply the exact-local theorem to each representation.
Both give the same graph-theoretic local connectivity lambda_G(c,f).
Thus both matching numbers equal lambda_G(c,f)-1.

representation_invariant.name: EXACT_CHANNEL_CAPACITY
representation_invariant.representation_formula: rho_G(c,f)=nu(X) for every exact-channel representation of anchors (c,f).
representation_invariant.dependence: Depends only on G and the ordered/unordered anchor pair, not on the hub, partition, ports, or chosen lattice solution.

fixed_anchor_pair: Run graph-only exact-channel discovery over eligible hubs z for the fixed anchors c,f.
Stop at the first feasible triple (z,c,f).
Use the canonical minimal-R solution R_min=Reach_D(R0).
Reconstruct canonical ports and channel graph X_min.
Compute a maximum matching M and minimum vertex cover U in X_min.
Then k=nu(X_min)=rho_G(c,f), and this is the matching capacity of every exact-channel representation of the same anchor pair.
proof_carrying_receipt: feasible reachability triple and canonical R_min

lattice_consequence.statement: The decomposition lattice controls representation geometry but not channel matching capacity.
lattice_consequence.bottom_solution_suffices: The canonical bottom R_min suffices to compute the exact capacity.

hub_consequence.statement: The hub is not part of the capacity invariant.
hub_consequence.qualification: Different hubs may yield different partitions and different channel edge sets, but for the same anchors all valid channel graphs have the same nu.

algorithmic_firewall.fixed_anchor_pair: The first feasible hub/partition suffices for capacity of that anchor pair.
algorithmic_firewall.whole_graph: If a future task asks to optimize or compare rho_G(c,f) over different anchor pairs, one must still examine/optimize over anchor pairs; capacities of distinct anchor pairs need not agree.
algorithmic_firewall.stronger_semantics: Additional C11/source-role restrictions may restrict which representations are admissible and must be audited separately.

exhaustive_small_graph_sanity_check.scope: Grouped all valid exact-channel decompositions by graph and anchor pair, including different hubs and partitions.
exhaustive_small_graph_sanity_check.authority: SANITY_CHECK_ONLY; theorem authority is the exact-local formula.

pipeline_sharpening.fixed_anchor_pipeline: G,(c,f) -> first feasible reachability decomposition -> canonical X_min -> nu(X_min)=rho_G(c,f) -> lambda_G(c,f)=rho+1 -> optional global kappa certification
removed_steps: enumeration of the full decomposition lattice
optimization over feasible partitions for fixed anchors
optimization over hubs for fixed-anchor channel capacity
